posts.title: What Changed as the New GitHub Dashboard Became Default - Features in the Changelog and How to Revert
posts.description: GitHub set its new dashboard as default for everyone. We review changelog details on agent sessions, 12-item limits, Feed separation, and the Preview switch.

posts.title: The Real Problem with Autonomous Driving Data Is Not Size — Three Problems of Time, Rarity and Reproducibility, and Preserving Meaning
posts.description: Reads the time, rarity and reproducibility problems in Sangmin Yoon’s autonomous driving data post through its figures and math, noting what it leaves unsaid.

posts.title: What Numbers Exposed Under Redaction in Nebraska Data Center Reports Reveal and Conceal
posts.description: A close reading of the news report on redacted Nebraska data center filings: Agate’s power and water figures, three sites’ tax refund estimates, and the math.

posts.title: Shortening Dependency Wait Times in Rust Builds With headstart - Conditions and Prototype Limits
posts.description: We analyze headstart, which emits early metadata so dependent Rust crates start sooner, and read its 16-core and 4-core results by system and project.

posts.title: What Deriving Inlines Reveals About Binary Size - uv 160KB Reduction and Compiler Trade-Offs
posts.description: We explain how Rust derives emit implicit inline, how uv saved about 160KB by blocking one Debug inline, and what rustc PRs 117727 and 118031 recorded.

posts.title: The AI-Native SDLC Six-Stage Blueprint — Artifact-Driven Feedback Loops and Strategic Human Oversight
posts.description: Anthropic's AI-native SDLC playbook turns linear handoffs into a loop of committed artifacts. We cover six stages, hook approval gates, and what humans keep.

posts.title: Claude Code Mods Architecture and Hook Extensions — Session-Resident Design and Security Boundaries
posts.description: Claude Code mods are JS/TS hook modules resident in a session. We cover the three hook moves, three official examples, and security advice for installing.

posts.title: In bash the Pipe Carries Text, in PowerShell It Carries Objects - grep, sort and uniq Equivalents and the 5.1 Traps
posts.description: bash pipes carry text; PowerShell pipes carry objects. Windows PowerShell 5.1 output maps ls|grep, sort|uniq -c, wildcards and curl or ls aliases, plus traps.

posts.title: PowerShell Error Handling Is More Than try/catch - Verified Exit Codes and $LASTEXITCODE
posts.description: PowerShell judges failure in three places: exceptions, $? and $LASTEXITCODE. Windows PowerShell 5.1 output shows what try/catch misses and exit code rules.

posts.title: Arguments PowerShell 5.1 Passes to External Programs Depend on the Quotes - Quoting and Escaping Traps Measured as argv
posts.description: Measured argv for what PowerShell 5.1 passes to git, python and curl.exe: lost empty strings, stripped quotes, trailing backslashes, splatting and --%.
